newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish bond market cautious on political turmoil.
newsitem.headline: Turkish bond market cautious on political turmoil.

text.p: Despite lira liquidity and relatively low funding costs, Turkish bond yields are floating in a narrow range due to politics and bankers say yields are unlikely to fall unless political uncertainties diminish.
"Demand for the closure of the Welfare Party (RP) has boosted uncertainties. For this reason, bond demand is weak in the market," a private bank dealer said.

A top prosecutor called on the Constitutional Court on Wednesday to outlaw Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamist RP for threatening the secularist Turkish state. Legal sources said any verdict would take at least six months.

Turkish lira liquidity, caused by the treasury's bill redemption of 61.03 trillion lira and the central bank's 85.5 trillion lira reverse repo repayment, has sent overnight money rates down by around 12-20 percentage points to 55-62 percent in the past two days.
However, bond demand has come under political pressure and yields stuck in a range of 98.5 and 100 percent.
Market players, scared by political uncertainties, are avoiding undertaking new bond positions, bankers say.
"The other factor deterring buyers is weak demand from the public," a banker said.
The treasury offered a nominal 110 trillion lira of 362 day t-bills with a yield of 97.54 percent to the public on Wednesday, but only 40 trillion lira worth of papers were sold.
A treasury official, who declined to named, said political turmoil and the availability of outstanding papers with the same maturity but higher return were the major reasons behind the low demand.
Bankers say buyers are also sidelined with expectations of a further rise in yields, citing at the treasury's continuing borrowing requirement.
However, the treasury official said some 100 trillion lira would be raised through value added tax and income withholding tax revenues this month.
The treasury will pay about 40 trillion lira in pensions later this month.
